In his 14-year [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) career, he played for the [[Miami Heat]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Washington Wizards]] and [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Butler was born in [[Philadelphia]], and raised in the [[Point Breeze, Philadelphia|Point Breeze]] area of South Philadelphia. After playing [[college basketball]] with the [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle Explorers]], he was drafted in the second round of the [[2002 NBA draft]] by the Heat. On January 31, 2018, Butler was behind the wheel when he and his girlfriend, [[Leah LaBelle]], died in a single vehicle car crash in Los Angeles. ==Early life== Butler was born as Felix Rasual Cheeseborough to parents Felix Cheeseborough and Cheryl Taylor. When he was aged eight, his father was murdered on a [[South Philadelphia]] street in an unsolved case. Taylor changed her son's name to Rasual Butler using her mother's [[maiden name]] so Butler would not be constantly reminded of his father's death. ==College career== Butler played his college career with the [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle Explorers]]. He became the sixth Explorer to score over 2,000 points, and at the time of his induction into the La Salle University Hall of Athletes, he ranked fourth among the Explorer's all-time scorers (2,125). He was named to First Team All-Atlantic 10 (2001, 2002) and was selected to the Verizon Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Championship All-Tournament team in 2002. He was inducted into the La Salle Hall of Athletes in 2008.{{cite web|last1=Neubeck|first1=Kyle|title=Former La Salle star Rasual Butler dead at 38 following car crash|url=http://www.phillyvoice.com/former-la-salle-star-rasual-butler-dead-38-following-car-crash/|website=Philly Voice|date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=February 1, 2018}} ==Professional career== === Miami Heat (2002–2005) === Butler was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] with the 53rd pick of the [[2002 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=2002 NBA Draft|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/nba_draft_history/2002.html|work=NBADraft.net|access-date=March 12, 2016|archive-date=February 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201133840/http://www.nbadraft.net/nba_draft_history/2002.html|url-status=dead}} === New Orleans Hornets (2005–2009) === After three seasons with the Heat, Butler was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] as part of the largest trade in NBA history. The four-team trade involved the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], Miami Heat, [[Boston Celtics]], and [[Utah Jazz]], and featured 13 players, most notably [[Eddie Jones (basketball)|Eddie Jones]], [[Antoine Walker]], [[Jason Williams (basketball, born 1975)|Jason Williams]] and [[James Posey]].{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2005-08-02-five-team-trade_x.htm|title=Walker to Heat in five-team, 13-player megadeal|work=[[USA Today]]|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|date=August 2, 2005|access-date=May 22, 2014}} During the 2007–08 regular season, Butler averaged 17 minutes of action, 4.9 points and 2 rebounds per game while coming mostly from the bench.{{cite web|title=Rasual Butler 2007-08 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/butlera01/gamelog/2008/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 12, 2016}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2009–2011) === [[File:Rasual Butler 2009.jpg|thumb|right|Butler with the Clippers in 2009]] On August 12, 2009, the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] acquired Butler by trading a conditional 2016 second round draft pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090812.html|title=Clippers Acquire Rasual Butler From New Orleans|work=NBA.com|date=August 12, 2009|access-date=August 12, 2009}} He was waived by the Clippers on February 28, 2011.{{cite news|title=CLIPPERS WAIVE BUTLER|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/110228.html|access-date=February 28, 2011|work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2011}} === Chicago Bulls (2011) === Butler signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on March 3, 2011.{{cite news|title=BULLS SIGN FREE AGENT RASUAL BUTLER|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/butler_signed_110302.html|access-date=March 3, 2011|work=NBA.com|date=March 3, 2011}} === Toronto Raptors (2011–2012) === In August 2011, Butler signed a one-year contract with [[CB Gran Canaria]].{{cite news|title=CB Gran Canaria lands former Bulls Rasual Butler|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88174/cb-gran-canaria-lands-former-bulls-rasual-butler.html|access-date=August 22, 2011|work=Sportando.com|date=August 22, 2011}} However, he never made an appearance for them on the court. On December 10, 2011, Butler signed a new contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20111210/21915/raptors-sign-free-agent-forward-rasual-butler|title=Raptors Sign Free Agent Forward Rasual Butler|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=December 10, 2011|access-date=December 11, 2011}} He was waived by the Raptors on March 23, 2012. He averaged 3.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 13 minutes of action in 34 games.{{cite news|title=Raptors waive Rasual Butler|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7729352/toronto-raptors-waive-forward-rasual-butler|access-date=March 23, 2013|work=ESPN.com|date=March 23, 2013}} === Tulsa 66ers (2013) === On January 18, 2013, Butler joined the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite news|title=Tulsa Acquires Guard Rasual Butler|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4535796|access-date=January 18, 2013|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 18, 2013}} He was subsequently named the 2013 Impact player of the Year, which is awarded to a player who joined an NBA D-League team midway through the season and made the greatest contribution following his in-season acquisition.{{cite news|title=Tulsa's Rasual Butler Earns 2013 NBA Development League Impact Player of the Year Award|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/butler_wins_impact_player_2013_04_19.html|access-date=April 19, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=April 19, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513174624/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/butler_wins_impact_player_2013_04_19.html|archive-date=May 13, 2013}} === Indiana Pacers (2013–2014) === On September 27, 2013, Butler signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite tweet|user=ScottAgness|author=Scott Agness|number=383600621867134978|date=September 27, 2013|title=Pacers have officially signed @RasualButler45 and Hilton Armstrong. They'll have 17 in camp. Full roster}}{{cite news|title=Pacers sign Hilton Armstrong|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/106393/pacers-sign-hilton-armstrong.html|access-date=September 27, 2013|work=Sportando.com|date=September 27, 2013}} He averaged 2.7 points, 0.8 rebounds and 0.3 assists in 50 games.{{cite web|title=Rasual Butler 2013-14 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/butlera01/gamelog/2014/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 12, 2016}} === Washington Wizards (2014–2015) === On September 29, 2014, Butler signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite news|title=Wizards Sign Six for Training Camp|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-six-training-camp|access-date=September 29, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2014}} After an impressive preseason and a fractured wrist suffered by [[Bradley Beal]], Butler made the final team prior to the start of the 2014–15 season. Within six regular season games, he was a force off the bench as he cemented a role under coach [[Randy Wittman]].{{cite news|title=Rasual Butler's stunning resurgence leads to guaranteed contract|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wizards-insider/wp/2015/01/09/rasual-butlers-stunning-resurgence-leads-to-guaranteed-contract/|access-date=January 9, 2015|work=WashingtonPost.com|date=January 9, 2015}} === San Antonio Spurs (2015–2016) === On September 28, 2015, Butler signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite news|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2015-16 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2015-16-training-camp-roster|access-date=September 28, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2015}} Butler's final NBA game was played on March 8, 2016, in a 116 - 91 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] where he played for 5 minutes and recorded no stats. The very next day on March 9, 2016, he was waived by the Spurs. He averaged 2.7 points, 1.2 rebounds and 9.4 minutes in 46 games.{{cite news|title=SPURS WAIVE RASUAL BUTLER|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-waive-rasual-butler|access-date=March 9, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=March 9, 2016}} On September 26, 2016, Butler signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],{{cite news|title=TIMBERWOLVES ANNOUNCE 2016-17 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-announce-2016-17-training-camp-roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}} but was waived on October 22 after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite news|title=TIMBERWOLVES WAIVE BUTLER, MURRY|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-butler-murry|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}} ==BIG3== In 2017, Butler was signed by the [[Ball Hogs]] to play in the [[BIG3]]. During the season, he was traded to the [[Dallas Power]].{{cite news|title=TRADE ALERT: Power acquires Rasual Butler From Ball Hogs|url=https://big3.com/news/item/98-trade-alert-power-acquires-rasual-butler-from-ball-hogs|work=Big3.com|date=July 25, 2017|access-date=April 14, 2018}} == Player profile == Butler's outside shooting was considered to be his greatest strength, shooting 36 percent over the course of his career and even 46 percent (50 total) during the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]] from behind the [[three-point field goal|three-point]] line.{{cite web|title=Rasual Butler 2003-04 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/butlera01/gamelog/2004/|access-date=March 12, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}} His career-high total were 134 made three-point shots (37 percent) during the [[2006–07 NBA season]].{{cite web|title=Rasual Butler 2006-07 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/butlera01/gamelog/2007/|access-date=March 12, 2016|work=Basketball-Reference.com}} ==Personal life== Butler had one adult daughter, Raven, who he lived with at the time of his death.{{Cite web |last=Robertson |first=Justin |title='He Was an Underdog:' the Inspiring Life and Puzzling Death of Rasual Butler |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2865738-he-was-an-underdog-the-inspiring-life-and-puzzling-death-of-rasual-butler |access-date=January 31, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} He starred in [[Trina]]'s music video "[[Here We Go (Trina song)|Here We Go]]".{{cite magazine|last=Whitaker |first=Land |title=NBA Antics |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/lang_whitaker/04/17/nba.oddities/ |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 17, 2006 |access-date=April 17, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024194453/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/lang_whitaker/04/17/nba.oddities/ |archive-date=October 24, 2012 }} Butler was close friends with fellow NBA player [[Lamar Odom]] and was seen in episodes of his television show ''[[Khloé & Lamar]]''.{{cite web|title='Khloe & Lamar' Star Rasual Butler & Wife Leah LaBelle Killed In Car Crash|url=https://okmagazine.com/news/rasual-butler-wife-leah-labelle-killed-in-car-crash/|website=OK! Magazine|date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=February 1, 2018}} ==Death== On January 31, 2018, Butler and his [[Common-law marriage|partner]] (initially misidentified as his wife),{{cite news |title=NBA player Rasual Butler and R&B singer Leah LaBelle killed in car crash |last=McCausland |first=Phil |date=January 31, 2018 |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/sports/nba-player-rasual-butler-r-b-singer-leah-labelle-die-n843456 |access-date=January 30, 2023}} singer [[Leah LaBelle]], were killed instantly in a high-speed car accident in the [[Studio City, Los Angeles|Studio City]] neighborhood of [[Los Angeles]], California, after he lost control of his [[Range Rover]] on [[Ventura Boulevard]] and crashed violently into a [[strip mall]] parking lot.{{cite news|last=Bloom |first=Tracy |title=Ex-L.A. Clippers Player Rasual Butler, Wife Killed in Violent, High-Speed Crash in Studio City |url=http://ktla.com/2018/01/31/man-woman-killed-in-violent-high-speed-crash-in-studio-city-police/ |work=[[KTLA]] |date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=January 31, 2018}} Autopsy reports showed traces of [[methamphetamine]], [[oxycodone]] and marijuana in Butler's body, and a [[blood alcohol content]] of 0.118%.{{cite magazine |title=Rasual Butler, Leah LaBelle Had Meth, Alcohol in Systems at Time of Death |first=Nicholas |last=Hautman |date=June 1, 2018 |magazine=[[Us Weekly]] |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/rasual-butler-leah-labelle-autopsy-results-show-meth-alcohol/#:~:text=Rasual%20Butler%20and%20Leah%20LaBelle%20had%20meth%20and,Angeles%20County%20coroner%E2%80%99s%20office.%20Celebrity%20Deaths%20in%202018
